title: Basin reserve-web vegetation guild
scope: Functional seasonal architecture of a major but non-exclusive open-ground vegetation guild in Project Hearthway's initial basin; usable within shared-setting ecology, geography, culture, economy, and story development.
claims: A reserve-web guild is a major but non-exclusive component of the initial basin's open-ground vegetation.
The guild contains multiple vegetation forms rather than one species or one continuous basin-wide organism.
Guild members maintain living subsurface networks that store water and nutrients and help them persist through winter, surface fire, episodic flooding, and grazing.
The guild produces tender spring growth, tall fibrous summer structures, and autumn fruiting or storage bodies.
Crown herds consume mature structural growth from the guild, while ribbon groups selectively harvest young growth and seasonal reproductive structures.
Browsing and trampling can create openings within reserve-web stands and the wider vegetation mosaic.
Excessive or repeated pressure can exhaust stored reserves and kill the living network; reserve-web regrowth is finite rather than automatic.
boundaries: The exact number, taxonomy, ancestry, names, and degree of convergence among guild members remain undefined.

Functional colony organization and local resource sharing are governed separately by canon://world/shared-universe-001/ecology/basin-reserve-web-modular-colonies; exact module anatomy, patch dimensions, connection density, transfer rates, growth, ageing, and reproduction remain undefined.
Primary energy capture, gas exchange, soil, mineral, water, temperature, and Mana requirements remain undefined.
Exact seasonal timing, productivity, nutrient content, chemistry, toxins, and defensive compounds remain undefined.
Fire, flood, frost, drought, grazing, disease, and pest tolerances and recovery rates remain undefined.
Distribution across soils, slopes, shorelines, wetlands, clearings, and corridors remains undefined.
Complementary vegetation, fungi or analogues, decomposers, parasites, mutualists, and human uses remain undefined.
Earth organisms may inform author-facing design but no living, extinct, or mythological Earth species is directly transplanted as an in-world guild member.
This record establishes no ambient spawning, automatic refill, guaranteed harvest, System reward, Skill, trait payload, specialised Mana ability, or Ancestry Development mechanic.
story_implications: Spring, summer, autumn, and winter present visibly different forage, cover, travel, and disturbance conditions.
Surface fire, flood, or grazing damage may leave living reserves below ground, but recovery can fail after repeated depletion.
Crown-herd browsing and trampling can help maintain openings until herd pressure exceeds the guild's recovery capacity.
Ribbon groups can track young growth and reproductive structures at a finer seasonal and spatial scale than crown herds.
Forage failure, delayed emergence, or exhausted reserves can affect herd condition and movement without acting as an arbitrary monster escalation.
system_implications: Reserve-web growth and recovery use finite stored and newly acquired matter and energy under CAL0 WLD2.1A+D.
The guild comprises ordinary biological member populations, not a spawn point, refill node, encounter reset, or guaranteed resource.
research_questions: How many species or lineages implement reserve-web strategies, and how are they related?
What structures store water and nutrients, and what controls module anatomy, patch size, and connection density?
How do modules and patches reproduce, disperse, fuse, fragment, reconnect, age, and compete?
Which soils, water regimes, slopes, and disturbance patterns favour each member?
What seasonal productivity and nutritional values can support ordinary crown and ribbon pressure?
Which pests, diseases, parasites, mutualists, and decomposers constrain the networks?
Which complementary vegetation guilds occupy woodland, wetland, shoreline, disturbed, and heavily grazed habitats?
Which human uses or management practices are biologically possible without establishing them culturally?
